column4: A certain man had two small children, a son and a daughter. The son was very good looking, the daughter was not more beautiful than usual. One day they were both playing near a looking-glass, and the boy said, ‘well, let us see in the glass which of us looks best.’ The girl disapproved of this thinking that he only said so in order to disgrace her. She then went to her father and complained of her brother. She said, ‘to feel satisfaction from looking into the glass is the business of women. Men should not give their mind to it.’ The father embraced them both, remonstrated with them, and said, ‘do not quarrel, my children. Henceforth you should both daily look in the glass.’
